page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results position this instance primarily in the middle tier for standard computing tasks. It achieves average performance in multi-core processing with a stress-ng score of 7398.32, software compilation with a Geekbench Clang score of 6735.0, and database operations with a PassMark database score of 2838.94. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 50.27 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, it exhibits weaker performance in single-core stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and specific workloads like ray tracing and image processing.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose workloads without the premium of specialized memory or compute-optimized tiers. Given its average performance in database operations, text processing, and static web serving with a 6.9 GB/sec throughput, the n2-standard-8 is suited for moderate web serving, software compilation, and standard database hosting. It is less optimal for compute-heavy physics simulations or graphics-related processing.

It features 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with hyperthreading) running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the n2-standard-8 in the average tier for most standard operations, including software compilation, database tasks, and static web serving, which registers a throughput of 6.9 GB/sec. However, it shows weaker results in single-core processing, multi-threaded decompression, and physics simulations. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a stable, cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, application hosting, and moderate database operations, rather than high-performance computing or graphics rendering.
